summary.headline: Elecon Q2 FY27 revenue rose 10.5% YoY to INR639 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 23.1%; FY27 guided to mid-double-digit growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue grew 10.5% YoY to INR639 crore, up 22.7% QoQ from INR521 crore, with EBITDA up 17.7% to INR148 crore and margin up 140 bps to 23.1%. Gear revenue rose 10.6% to INR488 crore, led by 30.3% overseas growth, while MHE revenue rose 10.4% to INR151 crore with MHE EBIT margin about 20.2% in Q2. Management attributed domestic softness to monsoon-related project slowness, steel price volatility and delayed project clearances, and said orders are firm and dispatch should pick up after Diwali. Management guided to medium double-digit consolidated revenue growth for H2 FY27 (around 15%) with minimum EBITDA margin at FY26 level.

segments.name: Gear division
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR488 crore (+10.6% YoY), EBIT INR108 crore at 22.1% margin (+290 bps); overseas growth 30.3% YoY. Catalog/engineered mix about 53%/47%; CP business about 50% of revenue, with limited pass-through of steel price changes.

segments.name: Material Handling Equipment (MHE)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR151 crore (+10.4% YoY); Q2 EBIT margin about 20.2% vs about 27% a year earlier, with H1 about 22.4%. Management guides 22-24% EBIT margin for FY27 and says project-to-project model limits raw material pass-through.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated revenue growth of medium double-digit for H2 FY27, cited as around 15%; guidance is on a consolidated basis and covers H2.
Minimum EBITDA margin to be maintained at FY26 level, out of caution; management expects H1 margin of 22.2% to be sustained.
MHE EBIT margin guided at 22-24% for FY27 and expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 as scale picks up.
Overseas revenue target of 50% of turnover by FY30 and INR5,000 crore consolidated top line by FY30, supported by organic growth and possible overseas acquisitions.
P-17 Bravo defence order: management expects RFP for final offer in Q2/Q3 FY28 and order award around Q1 FY29; Elecon expected to be single bidder as follow-on to P-17 Alpha.
Capex programme for three years remains on track; no specific capex amount given in call.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation at about 60% on a consistent basis; some machines are capacity-constrained and being debottlenecked with quarterly reassessment of machine additions.
Three-year capex programme stated as on track; no amount or timeline detail disclosed.
Gear and MHE: 2 MHE projects delayed in Q1 are now executing with good invoicing in Q2.
Management cites ultramodern manufacturing plant and R&D centre supporting customized and high-speed gearboxes.
demand_pricing: Gear domestic demand stable/soft in Q2; management attributes softness to delayed project execution due to monsoon and project clearances, and expects pickup after Diwali, especially till March.
Steel price volatility in last six months hit margins; Q1 raw material spike was abnormal, normalised in Q2 per management.
Overseas demand strong from Middle East and Americas; data centre, oil and gas and US references cited; Europe and UK improving slightly.
MHE competitors: TAKRAF and AUMUND (private sector); L&T and TKIL (EPC/BOP). TRF stated to have closed its material handling operations.
Industry: Indian heavy-duty industrial gearbox market expected to grow about 8% CAGR through FY30 (management estimate).

qa_highlights.question: What is driving domestic softness and what is the full-year growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Monsoon-related slowness and project execution delays; orders firm and executable, expected pickup post-Diwali. Guidance is mid-double-digit growth, around 15%, for H2, considering macro, geopolitical and inflation risks.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend in H2 given commodity inflation and product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 margin 22.2% expected to be maintained, with minimum at FY26 level. CP business (about 50% of revenue) has monthly price lists and less pass-through than engineered products.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MHE margin fall from about 27% to about 22%, and what happened to the power sector projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guides 22-24% MHE margin for FY27. Two delayed orders from Q1 are now executing with good Q2 invoicing; overseas margins slightly higher than domestic.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Gear margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes, better product mix and a bulk of export orders, which had been planned for Q1, executed in Q2 at higher margins. Gear 20-22% EBIT range now seen as achievable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the P-17 Bravo order timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Budgetary offers submitted; RFP for final offer expected Q2/Q3 FY28; order award expected Q1 FY29; execution 2-3 years. Elecon the single bidder as follow-on to P-17 Alpha.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR5,000 crore FY30 target and 50% overseas mix realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confident, citing organic growth, defence marine orders, heavy steel gearboxes, MHE exports and possible overseas acquisitions; no specific acquisition size given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the overseas order inflow and outstanding overseas order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 overseas order inflow INR230 crore vs INR172 crore a year earlier; H1 INR420 crore vs INR291 crore; overseas open order book INR326 crore. Management does not separate subsidiary and direct exports.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MHE EBIT margin decline in Q2 despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY26 had higher-margin orders; Q2 FY27 margin hit by order quality, early scale-up and weaker raw material price pass-through in project-based MHE. H1 MHE EBIT margin about 22.4%; margin to improve in Q3 and Q4.

risks_watch: Domestic gear demand softness and delayed project clearances; recovery after Diwali needs to show in Q3 revenue.
MHE margin at 20.2% in Q2 versus 22-24% guidance; watch Q3 margin recovery as scale builds.
Steel and raw material price volatility and rupee depreciation; CP business has limited price pass-through.
Overseas order inflow growth depends on Middle East, Americas and data centre demand; management declined to quantify H2 inflow.
P-17 Bravo timing has slipped in past calls; award now expected Q1 FY29.
Inorganic expansion planned in US and Europe; size and funding undisclosed.

But out of the abundant caution, we have said that we will be ha ving a minimum EBITDA margin percentage what we achieved in FY '26

summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth, order book and overseas strategy, but cautious on near-term domestic demand, guiding to around 15% H2 revenue growth and minimum FY26 EBITDA margin "out of abundant caution". Evasive on quantifying H2 overseas order inflow and on acquisition size; attributes domestic softness to monsoon and project clearance delays.

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 consolidated revenue growth of mid-double-digit (~15%), backed by open order books up 37% in Gear and 27% in MHE and a 60% utilisation with some machines debottlenecked; capex programme is on track but no amount or timeline given, so backing is only partial.
